messages:
anya: quick smokebench for borealis-11b int6 vs int4 — throwing up the topline so product/ops can decide.
sam: please paste the numbers, thanks.
mike: curious about sample size and slices too.
anya: results below (short run, ~2k tokens per model, mixed multi-turn + summarization slices):

```
model               | tokens/sec | p95 latency (ms) | unit $/1k tok | QA acc delta vs int6
borealis-11b-int6   | 125        | 210              | $0.72         | baseline
borealis-11b-int4   | 212        | 280              | $0.42         | -1.8%
```

anya: quick notes: int4 cuts unit cost ~42% and increases throughput, but p95 is higher due to increased decode variance on long context. QA accuracy drop concentrated on long multi-turn summarization slice (~-2.3%) and rare-entity recall (~-3.1%). other slices (short QA, math) are ~parity.
jade: what's the confidence? 2k tokens seems small for tails.
anya: agreed. bootstrap CI ~0.6% for overall QA delta; slice-level CIs wider. we saw consistent regression pattern across 3 seeds though.
sam: product ask — is user-visible degradation likely? numbers look small but long-form is core for a few customers.
mike: two risk profiles — latency-sensitive frontdoor apps (p95 matters) and cost-sensitive backfill jobs (throughput matters). int4 seems right for backfill and non-critical batched workloads.
anya: proposal:
- GA: keep int6 as default for hosted prod and GTN flows.
- Canary: shadow int4 at 5-10% for low-risk tenants (summaries disabled), measure online quality signals (click-through, rollups).
- Bulk jobs: route batch/embeddings-like workloads to int4 immediately with throttled concurrency.
- Eval: run 50k-token synthetic slice (long-form summarization + rare-entity) to pin CI and troubleshoot priming sensitivity.
- If int4 regression <= -0.5% overall and slice regressions < -1% after priming tweaks, consider 30% routing for non-latency flows.

sam: sounds conservative enough. can we get a quick runbook for rollback criteria?
jade: infra will need a feature flag and route-based split, and per-tenant fallback to int6. we can push a canary in 1 day.
anya: runbook draft:
- metrics to monitor: slice-precision, user-CTR, p95 latency, error-rate.
- rollback triggers: absolute drop in slice-precision > 1.5% for 30m OR overall QA drop >1% with p<0.05 OR user-CTR down >3% on canary cohort.
- mitigation: route canary traffic back to int6, increase caching/prefixing, enable kv-cache warmstart for int4 to see if p95 improves.

mike: also add automatic fallback if decode error rate > 0.5% (seen in an earlier int4 run).
anya: action items:
- saya/infra: create canary flag + split (jade) — ETA 24h.
- mike: run 50k-token eval sweep + priming variants (ETA 48h).
- anya: collect baseline slices and synth runs, publish scorecard (pass/fail) — ETA 36h.

sam: ok — product is okay with shadowing and batch routing. please ping once scorecard published. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary flag created: feature/eng-ml/borealis-int4-canary (assigned to jade).

jade: I'll wire the flag and add metrics dashboards (p95, slice_precision, fallback_rate). tagging infra alert thresholds as per runbook.
anya: thanks. will post scorecard link once available and drop recommended routing percentages.

sam: thanks team — good balance between cost wins and risk. we'll loop GTN after the 50k run.

mike: quick note — if priming recovers >1% on the long slice we should re-evaluate threshold for earlier rollout.
anya: agreed. I'll try 3 priming variants in the sweep and summarize.

sam: 👍
